description: The line plot illustrates the performance of different methods for multivariate anomaly detection, as measured by the Area Under the Curve (AUC) in percent, across varying values of N (likely representing a parameter such as the number of neighbors, dimensions, or context length). The x-axis, labeled “N”, ranges from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and the y-axis, labeled “AUC (%)”, spans from 75% to 100% with tick marks every 5 percentage points. Five distinct lines, each with a unique color and marker shape, represent different configurations or baselines: the blue line with circle markers starts at ~94% at N=0, peaks at ~98.5% at N=5, remains flat until N=10, then declines to ~94% at N=20; the orange line with diamond markers begins at ~84% at N=0, rises steadily to ~95% at N=10, and plateaus slightly before ending at ~94% at N=20; the green line with star markers starts at ~86% at N=0, increases gradually to ~93% at N=10, and continues rising slightly to ~94% at N=20; the red line with square markers begins at ~87% at N=0, climbs to ~98.5% at N=10, then drops to ~91% at N=20; and the purple line with triangle markers remains flat at ~79% from N=0 to N=5, then sharply increases to ~97% at N=10, followed by a steep decline to ~82% at N=20. The plot suggests that performance is highly sensitive to the value of N and varies significantly across methods, with some achieving peak performance around N=10 while others degrade beyond that point.
